results.name: VeloCloud Orchestrator SQL Injection Vulnerability
results.description: VeloCloud Orchestrator (VCO) on-premises versions contain a critical SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with minimal privileges to escalate to superuser operator access. Any user with Enterprise Read Only role can exploit this flaw to access privileged internal functionality, potentially compromising the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the orchestrator and managed data. The vulnerability is actively exploited, with specific malicious IP addresses identified. Affected versions include VCO 5.2.x prior to 5.2.3.18, 6.1.x prior to 6.1.3.10, and 6.4.x prior to 6.4.2.12. Hosted and dedicated VCO instances were already patched. Immediate upgrade to fixed releases is recommended, along with restricting web interface access and monitoring for suspicious activity.

results.name: 2026 Year End Phishing Lures
results.description: As organizations approach year-end and fiscal close periods, employees face increased administrative activity in finance, HR, and IT departments. This heightened legitimate communication creates ideal cover for phishing campaigns. Attackers exploit year-end business processes by impersonating compensation adjustments, Q4 financial documents, access reviews, invoice follow-ups, and benefits statements. Multiple campaigns have been observed targeting organizations across sectors including aviation, telecommunications, manufacturing, real estate, technology, and financial services, with concentration in the Middle East. Attackers leverage SharePoint, Docusign, and Microsoft 365 themes, employing credential harvesting pages disguised as document-sharing portals. Generic protected-message lures prove effective by requiring minimal customization while appearing legitimate during busy periods when employees expect increased document requests and administrative deadlines.

results.name: ARTEX in the Wild: Storm-0940 Expands Targeting of IT and Software Vendors
results.description: Throughout October 2026, an actor utilizing ARTEX, an autonomous AI penetration-testing agent, targeted multiple IT and software vendors with attacks focused on identity providers including Okta, Entra, and Cognito. The activity overlaps with Storm-0940, a Chinese-state aligned actor involved in supply-chain attacks. Observed methodologies included mapping applications through JavaScript bundles and source maps, probing authentication mechanisms, manipulating OAuth callbacks, password-spraying corporate environments, abusing account recovery endpoints, and testing tenant isolation. Sessions lasted 24-30 hours with automatic IP rotation when blocked. The agent demonstrated agentic behavior through automated step chaining, output-based adaptation, and relentless iteration. Attacks featured coordinated bursts with unique user agents, one-second intervals between attempts, and targeting of software engineers across hundreds of users.

results.name: SEO Poisoning Campaign Delivers New Armorsteal Malware
results.description: In September 2026, an SEO poisoning campaign distributed Armorsteal malware through fake websites impersonating Chocolatey package manager and Microsoft Activation Scripts (MAS) tool. Victims searching for software installation commands were presented with malicious PowerShell scripts that deployed Python-based malware protected by Pyarmor. The malware consists of three main components: a remote access module that communicates with command-and-control servers and verifies RSA-2048 signatures on received tasks; a surveillance module that logs keystrokes, monitors clipboard activity, hijacks cryptocurrency wallet addresses, and captures screenshots; and an information stealer targeting browser data, Discord tokens, cryptocurrency wallets, seed phrases, passwords, and SSH keys. The campaign employed anti-analysis techniques including cloud provider detection and code obfuscation, with infrastructure changes observed throughout the monitoring period.

results.name: StealC Is Back, and This Time It's a RAT
results.description: Four months after Operation Endgame dismantled StealC in June, its seller returned in October with Stadia, a full-featured remote access trojan that incorporates StealC's code verbatim. Unlike its predecessor, Stadia offers comprehensive remote administration capabilities including hidden desktop control, live command shell, file explorer, process manager, and in-memory loader, with the original StealC stealer functioning as one of six modules. The operator targets former StealC customers by offering a free month on the top-tier subscription priced at $900 monthly. Analysis reveals the binary shares byte-for-byte code with StealC version 3.5, particularly the Chromium App-Bound Encryption helper. The agent communicates via plain HTTP to three hardcoded IP addresses, uses RC4 encryption with Base64 encoding, and establishes persistence through hidden scheduled tasks under C:\ProgramData\ with randomized directory names impersonating legitimate updaters. results.name: MythicRatatoskr: An Yggdrasil-enabled backdoor deployed in a UAC-0099-Sandworm collaboration
results.description: On July 16th, 2025, UAC-0099 conducted a spearphishing attack against a Ukrainian grain logistics company, deploying the MATCHWOK backdoor. The following day, attackers introduced MythicRatatoskr, a previously undocumented Go-based backdoor utilizing the Yggdrasil mesh network for command and control communications. This decentralized network enables end-to-end encrypted IPv6 traffic between nodes, complicating detection efforts. Approximately two months later, on September 17th, 2025, Sandworm executed a destructive data-wiping attack using the SDelete utility deployed via Active Directory Group Policy. This incident represents documented cooperation between UAC-0099, acting as an initial access broker, and Sandworm, responsible for the destructive phase. The MythicRatatoskr backdoor supports standard backdoor functionality including command execution, file transfer, screenshot capture, and SOCKS5 proxying capabilities, marking the first documented case of state-aligned actors exploiting Yggdrasil infrast...

results.name: Hunting Leaked PHP2Shell RCE Across Open Directories (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619)
results.description: Two critical PHP remote code execution vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both rated CVSS v4.0 9.2, leaked before their scheduled patch on October 21, 2026. The flaws involve out-of-memory corruption in PHP core through multipart/form-data parsing, exploitable via session.upload_progress without authentication. Scanning began approximately 20 minutes after the patch release, with activity traced to a Mirai-style IoT botnet. Analysis of attacker infrastructure revealed approximately ten workspaces staging php2shell tooling, targeting WooCommerce, WHMCS, and Magento platforms. Despite widespread exposure affecting over 683,000 IPs running vulnerable PHP versions, no successful in-the-wild exploitation was confirmed as of October 21, 2026. The technical difficulty of achieving reliable code execution on systems with address-space randomization limited successful compromises.
targeted_countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

results.name: M365 Token Spray and Replay Campaign Compromises Business Email Accounts
results.description: Between July and September 2026, a sophisticated campaign targeted Microsoft 365 accounts through adversary-in-the-middle attacks and token replay techniques. The operation captured sign-in sessions via AiTM relays and replayed stolen tokens from IP addresses controlled by German hosting provider 1337 Services GmbH. Over ten weeks, 79 organizations were compromised with 497 successful sign-ins against over 200,000 failed attempts. Attackers registered 48 rogue Entra devices, replaced victim MFA methods, and created hidden inbox rules to conceal malicious communications. The campaign evolved through four distinct phases, rotating through different IP addresses and employing both scripted token replay and browser session replay techniques. In one case, compromised accounts were used to send payroll-related emails to external contacts, demonstrating business email compromise objectives.

results.name: Inside SiriusQT: A Seriously Skilled RAT
results.description: SiriusQT is a Windows Remote Access Trojan advertised on dark web forums since April 2026, offering capabilities beyond remote administration including HVNC, credential theft, cryptocurrency wallet collection, clipboard monitoring, keylogging, process injection, and persistence mechanisms. Distributed via Malware-as-a-Service by a reseller named GhostKernel, at least 30 users purchased licenses ranging from monthly to lifetime access. The malware was observed targeting victims in the United Kingdom, Germany, France, Spain, Italy, and the Netherlands. SiriusQT employs custom encrypted command-and-control traffic, multiple process injection techniques, and features both native C++ and .NET loader variants. The threat actor Amonus is referenced as the alleged developer, though GhostKernel appears to be the primary distributor through underground forums and Telegram channels.

results.name: INC and The Gentlemen Ransomware: Exposed AI Infrastructure
results.description: Threat researchers discovered an AI-driven intrusion ecosystem operated by affiliates of INC Ransomware and The Gentlemen Ransomware groups through seven exposed command-and-control servers. The operators integrated commercial AI models via OpenCode and OpenRouter, logging over 8,000 messages across 133 sessions with recorded spending exceeding $23,000. They exploited edge devices at scale including FortiClient EMS, SimpleHelp, and cPanel systems, compromising thousands of targets. The infrastructure contained 46 custom INC encryptor builds staged for October 1, 2026 deployment, evidence of live victim encryption, and a custom arsenal including the Phantom autonomous framework, Ghost C2, and various exploitation tools. The campaign targeted 62 named organizations, predominantly in the United States, with focus on industrial manufacturing and healthcare sectors. OPSEC failures in late September 2026 exposed source code, credentials, AI session logs, and complete victim knowledge bases.
